1	# Proposal: KNB1 recovery bundle codec and member commitment
2	
3	This freezes the proposed byte/schema choices for independent design review of
4	`kan-v2-recovery-bundles.md`. It is not an implemented format. No writer may use
5	these bytes as a compatibility promise until the design and independent vectors
6	are reviewed. The parent bundle requirements and publication distinctions apply.
7	
8	## Identities and canonical values
9	
10	The physical database encoding is UTF-8. Creation must set `PRAGMA encoding =
11	'UTF-8'` before creating tables; opening must verify the existing encoding is
12	UTF-8 and refuse UTF-16 rather than attempting conversion. This is a proposed
13	format requirement; no creation/opener exists yet.
14	
15	The outer SQLite `application_id` is `0x4b4e4231` (KNB1), `user_version=1`.
16	The logical member is explicitly profile 2 or 3; its ordinary archive/scope/issuer
17	binding is preserved. An owner supplies an independently retained random 32-byte
18	bundle ID and observer DID key. Neither is learned as authority from the file.
19	A bundle backup preserves that ID; a new observation branch needs explicit owner
20	selection or a new bundle identity, not a silent history merge.
21	
22	Canonical DAG-CBOR and low-S P-256 signature encoding follow the already reviewed
23	service-attestation codec, with a separate signature domain and a separate closed
24	schema. Integers are nonnegative and at most `9007199254740991`. Identifiers use
25	canonical CID encoding (raw/SHA256 for object bytes; DAG-CBOR/SHA256 for statements)
26	and validated static `did:key` P-256 authors. Unknown fields, alternate encodings,
27	unknown versions/events, malformed/non-low-S signatures and trailing bytes refuse.
28	A rejected record is not skipped while continuing the observation frontier.
29	
30	The envelope is the canonical DAG-CBOR map `{statement: bytes, signature: bytes}`.
31	The statement bytes encode exactly:
32	
33	- `version`: 1.
34	- `domain`: `tools.kan.recovery.observation.v1`.
35	- `bundle`: 32 bytes, the external physical-copy pin.
36	- `profile`: 2 or 3, the logical archive profile.
37	- `archive`, `scope`: 32 bytes each; `issuer`, `observer`: canonical DID strings.
38	- `sequence`: positive integer; `previous`: statement CID or null at genesis.
39	- `sampledAt`: Unix milliseconds, informational rather than ordering authority.
40	- `event`: one closed event name below; `body`: its closed event map.
41	
42	Compute the statement CID from its exact canonical bytes. Sign the canonical
43	DAG-CBOR preimage map `{domain: "tools.kan.recovery.observation.v1", statement:
44	<statement CID link>}` using the existing P-256 identity signer. This follows the
45	service proof's domain-separated CID preimage pattern, with a different domain.
46	The statement's domain field must equal that same literal. The statement CID
47	hashes statement bytes, not the envelope/signature. Envelope maximum
48	16 KiB includes both encoded byte strings. Every body repeats the complete pinned
49	context through the common statement; no observation inherits an unverified
50	identity from an earlier row.
51	
52	## Initial member commitment M1
53	
54	`SHA256` consumes the following byte stream. `F(x)` means an unsigned 64-bit
55	big-endian byte length followed by x. `N(n)` is unsigned 64-bit big-endian n.
56	The pure framing layer bounds issuer text to 1..80 UTF-8 bytes; it does not
57	validate a DID. A full member requires a canonical static P-256 DID (56..80
58	ASCII bytes), a stricter semantic check. DIDs use UTF-8; CID frames use canonical binary CID bytes; record/envelope frames
59	use exact original canonical bytes. Empty sections still include their count.
60	
61	1. ASCII `tools.kan.recovery.member.v1` followed by one zero byte.
62	2. `N(profile)`, `F(archive)`, `F(scope)`, `F(issuer)`.
63	3. `F("plan")`, `N(0)` for profile 2. Profile 3 instead has `N(1)`,
64	   `F(exact original plan envelope)`.
65	4. `F("original-membership")`, `N(count)`, then canonical object-CID text lexical
66	   order: `F(binary CID)`, `N(expected length)`. Profile 2 has zero entries.
67	5. `F("records")`, `N(count)`, then increasing contiguous sequence:
68	   `N(sequence)`, `F(manifest bytes)`, `F(receipt bytes)`, `F(issuer proof bytes)`.
69	6. `F("original-objects")`, `N(count)`, then canonical object-CID text lexical
70	   order: `F(binary CID key)`, `N(actual retained byte length)`, `F(raw bytes)`.
71	
72	The original object key is retained even when its raw bytes do not hash to it.
73	Missing objects are absent, not fabricated empty rows. A present zero-length
74	corrupt object is a present row with length zero and an empty frame. Staged/orphan
75	objects are included. A valid identifier with corrupted bytes is representable;
76	a malformed key, duplicate logical key, unreadable SQL cell, unknown schema or
77	non-BLOB object cell (including TEXT with identical encoded bytes), or
78	raw object larger than 4 MiB refuses initial creation and retains the source and
79	failed output. This is a bounded capture format, not arbitrary SQLite forensics.
80	A later format for oversized forensic fragments needs a separate explicit recipe;
81	it must not silently truncate a row to fit M1.
82	
83	M1 intentionally excludes rebuildable indexes/lookup columns, bundle identity,
84	observations and restoration candidates. Those are bound by their own signed
85	context/history. Identical member evidence in two physical bundles has the same
86	M1. The source metadata frontier includes both manifest and issuer-statement CIDs,
87	not just a high-water sequence. For empty history both are null.
88	
89	## Event bodies
90	
91	All digests below are 32 bytes; `member` uses M1, `output` uses O1, and
92	`restorations` uses R1. O1 has exactly M1 framing with the initial domain replaced
93	by ASCII `tools.kan.recovery.output.v1` followed by a zero byte. It commits to the
94	fully verified selected output rather than the original damaged member. All attempt IDs are owner-generated
95	16-byte values. A `frontier` is a closed map `{through, manifest, attestation}`
96	with both links null iff `through=0`. Nonempty links have DAG-CBOR/SHA256 codec.
97	
98	- `created`: `{recipe: 1, member: digest, frontier}`. Exactly sequence 1; no later
99	  created event. The logical metadata/proof chain must independently verify.
100	- `unavailable`: `{member: digest, entries: [...]}`. One to 32 entries, each
101	  `{occurrence, cid, expectedLength, state}`. `occurrence` is a positive member
102	  sequence or null for a staged/orphan object; `expectedLength` is an expected
103	  length from authenticated metadata/membership or null only for an unreferenced
104	  staged/orphan object without an authenticated length, in either profile. `state` is `missing` or
105	  `corrupt`. No metadata-corruption state pretends a broken proof is trustworthy.
106	- `restored`: `{member: digest, cid, length, candidate}`. `candidate` is the raw/SHA256 CID of the
107	  verified candidate and equals `cid`; length is 1..4 MiB. The target must exist
108	  in member metadata, original membership or original object keys. Any known
109	  expected lengths must agree; conflicting references refuse. Unknown orphan
110	  length is established by this verified candidate, not invented historical data.
111	- `publication-intent`: `{attempt, member: digest, restorations: digest,
112	  output: digest, frontier}`. `output` is the expected O1 of the deterministic
113	  selected standalone output, checked before signing intent. Exactly one intent
114	  per attempt ID. No path/command is trusted as signed executable routing data.
115	- `publication-observed`: `{attempt, intent, output: digest, frontier}`. `intent`
116	  cites the exact prior intent statement. `output` is O1 of the fully verified
117	  standalone output, must equal the cited intent output commitment, using selected valid objects and unchanged original metadata.
118	  It reports an observed durable output; it never records service activation.
119	- `publication-failed`: `{attempt, intent, reason}`. Closed reason enum:
120	  `source-changed`, `invalid-candidate`, `destination-conflict`, `budget`, `io`,
121	  `verification`. It makes no assertion that an output file does not exist.
122	
123	The 32-entry limit is subordinate to the 16 KiB envelope bound. Use another
124	linked observation when encoding would exceed that bound. All created/member
125	references must equal the independently recomputed original M1. Unavailable
126	entries must match the sampled original rows and authenticated expected
127	coordinates; restoration never deletes them. Restore and publication events
128	must reference the member fixed at creation, not a silently revised member.
129	
130	R1 is `SHA256(domain || N(count) || items)`, where domain is ASCII
131	`tools.kan.recovery.restorations.v1` plus zero byte, and items in canonical CID
132	text lexical order are `F(binary CID) || N(length) || F(candidate bytes)`.
133	R1 includes every candidate with a matching restored observation strictly before
134	that intent's sequence. There is no optional unsigned selection list. Each must
135	verify against its content address and all known expected lengths. A verifier
136	replays the chain to reconstruct this exact historical set; candidates appended
137	after the intent never enter its R1. A different candidate set requires a new
138	attempt and intent. This makes restart verification independent of a lost job
139	process or an externally remembered subset.
140	
141	The virtual standalone output contains exactly the union of original object
142	keys, authenticated record object references and original membership keys.
143	Every key needs verified bytes of all known expected lengths: use its verified
144	restoration candidate from this R1 set when present, otherwise its valid original
145	bytes. A still-missing/corrupt key refuses publication, including staged/orphan
146	keys. Never drop a corrupt orphan to make verification pass, add an unreferenced
147	new object, or use a candidate recorded after the intent. Recompute expected
148	output O1 from this deterministic union and unchanged records/plan/membership; both intent and
149	publication-observed must equal it and the original metadata frontier. The normal
150	standalone verifier still independently validates all signatures and profile
151	completion. A partial profile-3 member has no KNB1 publication operation; it stays
152	a retained recovery artifact until a separate metadata-extension design exists.
153	
154	## Exact initial loss coverage
155	
156	Derive one expected coordinate for each `(occurrence sequence, object CID)` in
157	member metadata. A shared CID used by two occurrences yields two distinct
158	coordinates, not a collapsed history. Add a null-occurrence coordinate for each
159	original membership key or original object key that has no occurrence reference;
160	never add a second null entry for a CID already represented by occurrences.
161	All authenticated lengths for a CID must agree or creation refuses. The expected
162	length is that agreed value, or null only for an unreferenced original object
163	without an authenticated length.
164	
165	Sample each coordinate against the original member objects. Missing rows produce
166	missing entries; wrong length/hash produces corrupt entries; available entries
167	produce no unavailable event. Non-BLOB cells refuse creation under the M1 rule.
168	Sort occurrence entries first by ascending numeric sequence then canonical CID
169	text; sort null entries last by canonical CID text. No duplicate coordinate is
170	allowed. The concatenation of creation's unavailable events must equal this exact
171	ordered loss vector: omissions, extra entries, duplicate entries, conflicting
172	states or altered expected lengths refuse verification.
173	
174	These events occur immediately after created, before restoration/publication.
175	Partition greedily into the largest consecutive prefix of at most 32 entries
176	whose canonical signed envelope fits 16 KiB; signatures have fixed 64-byte width.
177	No empty event is permitted. Empty loss coverage means created alone. Verifiers
178	recompute the same vector and partition; an unavailable event after that initial
179	coverage is invalid. Damage to the physical bundle after creation is an integrity
180	failure against its fixed M1, not permission to rewrite member bytes or insert a
181	new claim that retrospectively changes the initial sample. Preserve such media
182	and recover the bundle from verified backups; arbitrary forensic repair remains
183	outside KNB1.
184	
185	## Physical tables
186	
187	All tables use the exact frozen column order; any extra table/index/trigger/view
188	refuses normal bundle open. DDL must be generated once by the implementation and
189	pinned by canonical schema fixtures before a writer is accepted.
190	
191	- `bundle_identity(singleton INTEGER PRIMARY KEY CHECK(singleton=1), bundle BLOB,
192	  observer TEXT, profile INTEGER, archive BLOB, scope BLOB, issuer TEXT)`.
193	  Byte-width/profile/DID validation is mandatory on read and before writes.
194	- `member_records(sequence INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, manifest BLOB, receipt BLOB,
195	  envelope BLOB)`: sequence positive, manifest/receipt each 1..65536 bytes,
196	  envelope 1..16384 bytes; all NOT NULL. No ordinary `commits` or `attestations`
197	  table exists in this outer format.
198	- `member_objects(cid TEXT PRIMARY KEY, bytes BLOB NOT NULL) WITHOUT ROWID`:
199	  original bytes 0..4194304, key canonical but payload may be corrupt.
200	- `member_plan(singleton INTEGER PRIMARY KEY CHECK(singleton=1), envelope BLOB
201	  NOT NULL)`: no rows for profile 2, exactly one 1..4096-byte row for profile 3.
202	- `member_membership(cid TEXT PRIMARY KEY, length INTEGER NOT NULL) WITHOUT ROWID`:
203	  profile 3 only, canonical CID and length 1..4194304.
204	- `observations(sequence INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, envelope BLOB NOT NULL)`:
205	  canonical contiguous observation chain, envelope 1..16384 bytes.
206	- `restored_objects(cid TEXT PRIMARY KEY, bytes BLOB NOT NULL) WITHOUT ROWID`:
207	  bytes 1..4194304 and exact content address. Every row must have one matching
208	  restoration observation; every restoration observation must have its candidate.
209	
210	SQL constraints enforce local type/size bounds; the verifier independently
211	checks all semantic/profile/cardinality/chain conditions. In particular, empty
212	observation history cannot convert a bundle into a standalone archive.
213	Publication constructs an entirely separate normal profile; changing a marker
214	or renaming a table never constitutes publication.
215	
216	## Required pre-implementation review
217	
218	Review the event state machine, all cross-file crash outcomes and the ability to
219	resume or record failure without rewriting history. Freeze actual DDL, canonical
220	positive/re-signed-negative vectors and an independent Python encoder/verifier
221	before storage mutations are implemented. Pin M1 and R1 against independently
222	constructed empty, staged, missing, corrupt, restored and partial-copy fixtures.
223	Whole-output verification must include ordinary writable schema, original writer
224	signatures, issuer proof chain and profile-3 completion; M1 alone proves none of
225	those properties. The observer can report evidence, but cannot grant admission,
226	erase historical loss or assert a fabricated complete source-copy recipe.
227	
228	### Publication state and replay rules
229	
230	An attempt ID has exactly one intent. It may have zero or more failed observations
231	and at most one observed publication. A failure is evidence of an unsuccessful
232	check, not a terminal assertion that no valid output exists. Explicit resume may
233	therefore append observed after failure when it verifies that same attempt's
234	selected commitment and owner-specified output. No failed or second observed
235	record may follow observed for that attempt. A changed selection or different
236	output identity requires a new attempt ID and intent. Independent verifiers must
237	validate these relationships from the complete observation chain, not a mutable
238	status column.
239	
240	Creation's single publication transaction includes a created event plus enough
241	unavailable events to cover every unavailable expected occurrence, every
242	missing/corrupt original-membership key (including unreferenced staged objects),
243	and every corrupt retained orphan row. Missing orphans with no surviving expected
244	coordinate cannot be invented. Exact repeated restoration is idempotent: return
245	the prior candidate/observation, without a new row or signature. A candidate
246	insert without its observation, or observation without its candidate, refuses.
247	
248	The owner-selected observation frontier is an external checkpoint, comprising
249	sequence and statement CID under the full bundle/observer binding. Verifiers
250	must prove that checkpoint belongs to the observed chain and distinguish it from
251	any later verified extension. A file cannot supply its own rollback-detection
252	checkpoint. No cross-copy anti-equivocation beyond the explicitly pinned chain
253	is claimed.
254	
255	### Checkpoints and multiple completed outputs
256	
257	Several attempt IDs may each reach publication-observed. Each creates a separate
258	physical standalone output with the member's logical archive identity; none
259	activates a service. The owner must select exactly one live writer and fence the
260	others through the separately authorized activation workflow. The bundle cannot
261	promise that privileged manual configuration obeyed that workflow.
262	
263	Every successful mutation/job result returns the verified observation frontier
264	(sequence plus statement CID and full binding), including a committed failure
265	observation. The owner verifies and durably retains it outside the bundle before
266	advancing the recovery UI's independently checkpointed status. On restart the
267	owner supplies the latest retained checkpoint; valid extensions are reported
268	separately until retained. A tail truncated after the latest external checkpoint
269	is not detectable. The online observer key can attribute new statements but does
270	not itself provide an independent tamper-evidence or non-equivocation witness.
271	An uncertain response may require explicit inspection and checkpoint advancement;
272	do not derive the external pin from the bundle being verified.
273	
274	### Scope-C follow-through before format acceptance
275	
276	The governing bundle design's "custody and owner-visible limits" section is part
277	of this codec contract: pre-open path checks cover all participating databases;
278	partial-copy restart provenance is external job state only; forensic-only source
279	cells are a named recovery gap; unrecoverable staged/orphan keys explicitly block
280	publication. None changes the byte recipes or adds a silently unsigned field to
281	the closed observation schema. Draft SQL and wire fixtures still require their
282	own independent review before acceptance or any storage writer.
283	
284	## First implementation checkpoint: observation authentication
285	
286	`src/evidence_recovery_observation.rs` implements only bounded canonical wire
287	validation, static P-256 owner pins, observer signature attribution and contiguous
288	observation predecessor links. `Authenticated` has private construction and
289	carries no bundle-completeness, member-truth or publication-state authority.
290	`sign_claim` is a pure signer and round-trip validator; its caller must establish
291	the permitted operation and semantic truth before using it. There is no storage
292	consumer, mutation, file routing, checkpoint acceptance or browser API here.
293	
294	Independent Python fixtures exercise the six event forms, exact statement/CID/
295	signature bytes, maximum wire shapes and re-signed hostile cases. Their member,
296	restoration and output digest values deliberately do not establish a valid full
297	bundle. A wire-valid claim may still be false; complete bundle verification must
298	reject those false claims. The Rust API does not provide JSON serialization or
299	accept a caller-constructed predecessor as authenticated history.
300	
301	The accompanying SQL fixture is a **draft** local-constraint schema, exercised
302	in memory with no publication markers. The M1/O1/R1 Python oracle is a **draft**
303	framing oracle, not a signed-record or complete-member verifier; synthetic record
304	bytes in its framing cases do not qualify any archive. Neither draft is accepted
305	as a storage compatibility promise by this checkpoint. Before a bundle writer:
306	implement and independently qualify streaming commitment computation, complete
307	member/proof validation, exact loss partitioning, candidate/history consistency,
308	publication replay and external-checkpoint validation; then freeze their complete
309	cross-implementation vectors and DDL. All recovery writer/job/RPC/UI criteria stay
310	open until their real operations and crash outcomes are tested and reviewed.
311	
312	### Second independent review decisions
313	
314	Observer authority is a separate role and signature domain from archive issuer
315	authority. The wire codec permits explicitly pinned equal observer/issuer DIDs;
316	it never treats an observer signature as an archive proof. Distinct-key policy
317	belongs to owner configuration. Recovery job configuration should default to a
318	separate observer key and disclose explicit reuse; equality in the wire is not
319	proof of independent authorities or compromise isolation. This interpretation
320	of parent REQ-1 is recorded rather than silently requiring a new wire restriction.
321	The same-key role fixture pins this decision.
322	
323	Refusal reason strings in the cross-implementation fixtures identify their
324	single-fault cases. They do not define a total precedence for inputs with several
325	independent faults: Rust and Python may name different first faults while both
326	refuse. No authorization or state transition may depend on which diagnostic
327	string wins. Acceptance and byte identity remain the interoperability contract.
328	
329	The expanded fixtures now distinguish canonical CID text order from binary order
330	for unavailable entries, original membership, original objects and R1 candidates.
331	The draft DDL bounds identifier text by bytes, excludes embedded NUL and requires
332	printable ASCII; complete canonical DID/CID validation remains a verifier duty.
333	SQLite's lossless affinity coercion is not a promise about caller bind types:
334	writers must bind typed values and readers must still check stored types.
335	
336	An authenticated expected object length above 4 MiB also refuses KNB1 creation
337	as `forensic-recovery-required`, even when no oversized physical row survives.
338	Do not truncate the expected length or drop that reference to fit the format.
339	Retain source and failed output; the generic manifest schema's larger integer
340	range does not widen this proposed recovery format's representable object size.
341	
342	## Next checkpoint draft: bounded streaming framing
343	
344	The draft `evidence_recovery_commitment` module computes M1/O1/R1 incrementally.
345	Its caller supplies section counts and strictly increasing canonical CID-text
346	order; it does not allocate an archive-sized sort or payload buffer. Separate
347	membership/record/object stages enforce counts and contiguous record positions.
348	Any rejected builder operation poisons the builder, so ignoring an error cannot
349	produce a digest over fewer records. Empty corrupt originals remain representable;
350	restoration candidates must be nonempty and match their raw CID.
351	
352	Owner-selected item, work-byte, time and cancellation limits bound computation;
353	hashing polls at most every 64 KiB. Work-byte accounting includes framing and,
354	for restoration, both candidate verification and commitment hashing. It does not
355	bound prior caller acquisition or arbitrary filesystem stalls. The caller remains
356	responsible for authorized bounded source reads and complete member semantics.
357	DID/record/plan truth, candidate membership and full state replay are not supplied
358	by these framing digests. This draft has no storage consumer. Author qualification passes eight commitment
359	tests against independent Python vectors and nine compiled controls, with strict
360	v2 Clippy and formatting. Evidence is in
361	`.design/reviews/kan-v2-recovery-commitment-author/`. Fresh independent review
362	remains pending; full member and state verification are separate prerequisites.
363	
364	
365	### Streaming review follow-through
366	
367	Actual Opus 5.5 review of a8927a6 found no production defect and returned
368	APPROVE WITH FOLLOW-UPS; full raw evidence is retained in
369	`.design/reviews/kan-v2-recovery-commitment-opus/`. RA3/RA4 section/count/size
370	probes are promoted. Test-only cancellation injection qualifies polling within
371	hashing without timing sleeps; the original independent timing probe and its
372	recorded limits remain preserved. These follow-through tests pass author qualification: ten integration functions,
373	two deterministic polling units and thirteen compiled controls, plus strict
374	Clippy/format and the independent oracle. Evidence is in
375	`.design/reviews/kan-v2-recovery-commitment-followups-author/`. Fresh review with
376	the member-verifier checkpoint remains required.
377	
378	The 1..80-byte framing issuer bound is explicit above and now shared by the
379	Python oracle. UTF-8 is pinned for future physical creation and opening. An O1
380	digest from the framing builder alone still authenticates no output bytes:
381	full object/writer/profile verification must precede publication. None of these
382	changes accepts the physical format or closes parent acceptance criteria.
383	
384	## Next verifier checkpoint: logical member and initial availability
385	
386	The pure member verifier takes an owner-pinned context and borrowed, ordered
387	record, membership and original-object slices. Its caller must acquire those
388	bytes with bounded reads before calling; this is not a SQLite opener. The physical
389	reader must reject noncanonical original CID text before constructing typed CIDs;
390	parsing a spelling and silently normalizing it is not source validation. Explicit
391	item/input-byte/time/cancellation limits bound this invocation. It stores only
392	bounded metadata coordinates, never copies the whole payload collection. Hashing
393	polls per 64 KiB; canonical decoding, request verification and signatures are
394	individually bounded operations with cancellation checks around them.
395	
396	Independently verify the contiguous issuer chain, admitted versus retained-copy
397	purpose, static service writer form, per-writer position/predecessor, unique
398	operation, the service operation-to-slot commitment and consistent slot bindings. Profile 3 additionally binds its plan,
399	original membership and retained-prefix metadata digest. An unfinished prefix is
400	reported as incomplete; matching metadata alone does not certify missing writer
401	signatures or retained bytes. No standalone publication capability is returned.
402	
403	Every known length must be positive, at most 4 MiB, and agree across references
404	and original membership. Retain raw corrupt/empty originals in M1. Verify each
405	present object's hash once and sample every occurrence separately; unreferenced
406	membership/original keys receive null-occurrence loss coordinates. A hash-valid
407	request that fails its writer signature or exact manifest binding is invalid
408	member evidence, not a repairable missing-byte condition. Missing/corrupt requests
409	remain unavailable, with writer verification still outstanding. Loss output is
410	strict occurrence/CID-text order, followed by null coordinates in CID-text order.
411	
412	This checkpoint must be qualified before it can feed full observation replay.
413	Greedy signed-loss partitioning, historical restoration/output selection, replay,
414	checkpoints, physical schema and all storage mutations remain separate work.
415	
416	
417	The logical-member draft passes author qualification: 16 Rust functions,
418	independent signed Python fixtures, eight semantic controls (one additional
419	cancellation control survives because framing refuses later), strict Clippy and
420	formatting. Raw results are in
421	`.design/reviews/kan-v2-recovery-member-author/`. Fresh independent review is
422	pending; this is not full bundle acceptance.
423

# Proposal: KNB1 recovery bundle codec and member commitment

This freezes the proposed byte/schema choices for independent design review of
`kan-v2-recovery-bundles.md`. It is not an implemented format. No writer may use
these bytes as a compatibility promise until the design and independent vectors
are reviewed. The parent bundle requirements and publication distinctions apply.

## Identities and canonical values

The physical database encoding is UTF-8. Creation must set `PRAGMA encoding =
'UTF-8'` before creating tables; opening must verify the existing encoding is
UTF-8 and refuse UTF-16 rather than attempting conversion. This is a proposed
format requirement; no creation/opener exists yet.

The outer SQLite `application_id` is `0x4b4e4231` (KNB1), `user_version=1`.
The logical member is explicitly profile 2 or 3; its ordinary archive/scope/issuer
binding is preserved. An owner supplies an independently retained random 32-byte
bundle ID and observer DID key. Neither is learned as authority from the file.
A bundle backup preserves that ID; a new observation branch needs explicit owner
selection or a new bundle identity, not a silent history merge.

Canonical DAG-CBOR and low-S P-256 signature encoding follow the already reviewed
service-attestation codec, with a separate signature domain and a separate closed
schema. Integers are nonnegative and at most `9007199254740991`. Identifiers use
canonical CID encoding (raw/SHA256 for object bytes; DAG-CBOR/SHA256 for statements)
and validated static `did:key` P-256 authors. Unknown fields, alternate encodings,
unknown versions/events, malformed/non-low-S signatures and trailing bytes refuse.
A rejected record is not skipped while continuing the observation frontier.

The envelope is the canonical DAG-CBOR map `{statement: bytes, signature: bytes}`.
The statement bytes encode exactly:

- `version`: 1.
- `domain`: `tools.kan.recovery.observation.v1`.
- `bundle`: 32 bytes, the external physical-copy pin.
- `profile`: 2 or 3, the logical archive profile.
- `archive`, `scope`: 32 bytes each; `issuer`, `observer`: canonical DID strings.
- `sequence`: positive integer; `previous`: statement CID or null at genesis.
- `sampledAt`: Unix milliseconds, informational rather than ordering authority.
- `event`: one closed event name below; `body`: its closed event map.

Compute the statement CID from its exact canonical bytes. Sign the canonical
DAG-CBOR preimage map `{domain: "tools.kan.recovery.observation.v1", statement:
<statement CID link>}` using the existing P-256 identity signer. This follows the
service proof's domain-separated CID preimage pattern, with a different domain.
The statement's domain field must equal that same literal. The statement CID
hashes statement bytes, not the envelope/signature. Envelope maximum
16 KiB includes both encoded byte strings. Every body repeats the complete pinned
context through the common statement; no observation inherits an unverified
identity from an earlier row.

## Initial member commitment M1

`SHA256` consumes the following byte stream. `F(x)` means an unsigned 64-bit
big-endian byte length followed by x. `N(n)` is unsigned 64-bit big-endian n.
The pure framing layer bounds issuer text to 1..80 UTF-8 bytes; it does not
validate a DID. A full member requires a canonical static P-256 DID (56..80
ASCII bytes), a stricter semantic check. DIDs use UTF-8; CID frames use canonical binary CID bytes; record/envelope frames
use exact original canonical bytes. Empty sections still include their count.

1. ASCII `tools.kan.recovery.member.v1` followed by one zero byte.
2. `N(profile)`, `F(archive)`, `F(scope)`, `F(issuer)`.
3. `F("plan")`, `N(0)` for profile 2. Profile 3 instead has `N(1)`,
   `F(exact original plan envelope)`.
4. `F("original-membership")`, `N(count)`, then canonical object-CID text lexical
   order: `F(binary CID)`, `N(expected length)`. Profile 2 has zero entries.
5. `F("records")`, `N(count)`, then increasing contiguous sequence:
   `N(sequence)`, `F(manifest bytes)`, `F(receipt bytes)`, `F(issuer proof bytes)`.
6. `F("original-objects")`, `N(count)`, then canonical object-CID text lexical
   order: `F(binary CID key)`, `N(actual retained byte length)`, `F(raw bytes)`.

The original object key is retained even when its raw bytes do not hash to it.
Missing objects are absent, not fabricated empty rows. A present zero-length
corrupt object is a present row with length zero and an empty frame. Staged/orphan
objects are included. A valid identifier with corrupted bytes is representable;
a malformed key, duplicate logical key, unreadable SQL cell, unknown schema or
non-BLOB object cell (including TEXT with identical encoded bytes), or
raw object larger than 4 MiB refuses initial creation and retains the source and
failed output. This is a bounded capture format, not arbitrary SQLite forensics.
A later format for oversized forensic fragments needs a separate explicit recipe;
it must not silently truncate a row to fit M1.

M1 intentionally excludes rebuildable indexes/lookup columns, bundle identity,
observations and restoration candidates. Those are bound by their own signed
context/history. Identical member evidence in two physical bundles has the same
M1. The source metadata frontier includes both manifest and issuer-statement CIDs,
not just a high-water sequence. For empty history both are null.

## Event bodies

All digests below are 32 bytes; `member` uses M1, `output` uses O1, and
`restorations` uses R1. O1 has exactly M1 framing with the initial domain replaced
by ASCII `tools.kan.recovery.output.v1` followed by a zero byte. It commits to the
fully verified selected output rather than the original damaged member. All attempt IDs are owner-generated
16-byte values. A `frontier` is a closed map `{through, manifest, attestation}`
with both links null iff `through=0`. Nonempty links have DAG-CBOR/SHA256 codec.

- `created`: `{recipe: 1, member: digest, frontier}`. Exactly sequence 1; no later
  created event. The logical metadata/proof chain must independently verify.
- `unavailable`: `{member: digest, entries: [...]}`. One to 32 entries, each
  `{occurrence, cid, expectedLength, state}`. `occurrence` is a positive member
  sequence or null for a staged/orphan object; `expectedLength` is an expected
  length from authenticated metadata/membership or null only for an unreferenced
  staged/orphan object without an authenticated length, in either profile. `state` is `missing` or
  `corrupt`. No metadata-corruption state pretends a broken proof is trustworthy.
- `restored`: `{member: digest, cid, length, candidate}`. `candidate` is the raw/SHA256 CID of the
  verified candidate and equals `cid`; length is 1..4 MiB. The target must exist
  in member metadata, original membership or original object keys. Any known
  expected lengths must agree; conflicting references refuse. Unknown orphan
  length is established by this verified candidate, not invented historical data.
- `publication-intent`: `{attempt, member: digest, restorations: digest,
  output: digest, frontier}`. `output` is the expected O1 of the deterministic
  selected standalone output, checked before signing intent. Exactly one intent
  per attempt ID. No path/command is trusted as signed executable routing data.
- `publication-observed`: `{attempt, intent, output: digest, frontier}`. `intent`
  cites the exact prior intent statement. `output` is O1 of the fully verified
  standalone output, must equal the cited intent output commitment, using selected valid objects and unchanged original metadata.
  It reports an observed durable output; it never records service activation.
- `publication-failed`: `{attempt, intent, reason}`. Closed reason enum:
  `source-changed`, `invalid-candidate`, `destination-conflict`, `budget`, `io`,
  `verification`. It makes no assertion that an output file does not exist.

The 32-entry limit is subordinate to the 16 KiB envelope bound. Use another
linked observation when encoding would exceed that bound. All created/member
references must equal the independently recomputed original M1. Unavailable
entries must match the sampled original rows and authenticated expected
coordinates; restoration never deletes them. Restore and publication events
must reference the member fixed at creation, not a silently revised member.

R1 is `SHA256(domain || N(count) || items)`, where domain is ASCII
`tools.kan.recovery.restorations.v1` plus zero byte, and items in canonical CID
text lexical order are `F(binary CID) || N(length) || F(candidate bytes)`.
R1 includes every candidate with a matching restored observation strictly before
that intent's sequence. There is no optional unsigned selection list. Each must
verify against its content address and all known expected lengths. A verifier
replays the chain to reconstruct this exact historical set; candidates appended
after the intent never enter its R1. A different candidate set requires a new
attempt and intent. This makes restart verification independent of a lost job
process or an externally remembered subset.

The virtual standalone output contains exactly the union of original object
keys, authenticated record object references and original membership keys.
Every key needs verified bytes of all known expected lengths: use its verified
restoration candidate from this R1 set when present, otherwise its valid original
bytes. A still-missing/corrupt key refuses publication, including staged/orphan
keys. Never drop a corrupt orphan to make verification pass, add an unreferenced
new object, or use a candidate recorded after the intent. Recompute expected
output O1 from this deterministic union and unchanged records/plan/membership; both intent and
publication-observed must equal it and the original metadata frontier. The normal
standalone verifier still independently validates all signatures and profile
completion. A partial profile-3 member has no KNB1 publication operation; it stays
a retained recovery artifact until a separate metadata-extension design exists.

## Exact initial loss coverage

Derive one expected coordinate for each `(occurrence sequence, object CID)` in
member metadata. A shared CID used by two occurrences yields two distinct
coordinates, not a collapsed history. Add a null-occurrence coordinate for each
original membership key or original object key that has no occurrence reference;
never add a second null entry for a CID already represented by occurrences.
All authenticated lengths for a CID must agree or creation refuses. The expected
length is that agreed value, or null only for an unreferenced original object
without an authenticated length.

Sample each coordinate against the original member objects. Missing rows produce
missing entries; wrong length/hash produces corrupt entries; available entries
produce no unavailable event. Non-BLOB cells refuse creation under the M1 rule.
Sort occurrence entries first by ascending numeric sequence then canonical CID
text; sort null entries last by canonical CID text. No duplicate coordinate is
allowed. The concatenation of creation's unavailable events must equal this exact
ordered loss vector: omissions, extra entries, duplicate entries, conflicting
states or altered expected lengths refuse verification.

These events occur immediately after created, before restoration/publication.
Partition greedily into the largest consecutive prefix of at most 32 entries
whose canonical signed envelope fits 16 KiB; signatures have fixed 64-byte width.
No empty event is permitted. Empty loss coverage means created alone. Verifiers
recompute the same vector and partition; an unavailable event after that initial
coverage is invalid. Damage to the physical bundle after creation is an integrity
failure against its fixed M1, not permission to rewrite member bytes or insert a
new claim that retrospectively changes the initial sample. Preserve such media
and recover the bundle from verified backups; arbitrary forensic repair remains
outside KNB1.

## Physical tables

All tables use the exact frozen column order; any extra table/index/trigger/view
refuses normal bundle open. DDL must be generated once by the implementation and
pinned by canonical schema fixtures before a writer is accepted.

- `bundle_identity(singleton INTEGER PRIMARY KEY CHECK(singleton=1), bundle BLOB,
  observer TEXT, profile INTEGER, archive BLOB, scope BLOB, issuer TEXT)`.
  Byte-width/profile/DID validation is mandatory on read and before writes.
- `member_records(sequence INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, manifest BLOB, receipt BLOB,
  envelope BLOB)`: sequence positive, manifest/receipt each 1..65536 bytes,
  envelope 1..16384 bytes; all NOT NULL. No ordinary `commits` or `attestations`
  table exists in this outer format.
- `member_objects(cid TEXT PRIMARY KEY, bytes BLOB NOT NULL) WITHOUT ROWID`:
  original bytes 0..4194304, key canonical but payload may be corrupt.
- `member_plan(singleton INTEGER PRIMARY KEY CHECK(singleton=1), envelope BLOB
  NOT NULL)`: no rows for profile 2, exactly one 1..4096-byte row for profile 3.
- `member_membership(cid TEXT PRIMARY KEY, length INTEGER NOT NULL) WITHOUT ROWID`:
  profile 3 only, canonical CID and length 1..4194304.
- `observations(sequence INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, envelope BLOB NOT NULL)`:
  canonical contiguous observation chain, envelope 1..16384 bytes.
- `restored_objects(cid TEXT PRIMARY KEY, bytes BLOB NOT NULL) WITHOUT ROWID`:
  bytes 1..4194304 and exact content address. Every row must have one matching
  restoration observation; every restoration observation must have its candidate.

SQL constraints enforce local type/size bounds; the verifier independently
checks all semantic/profile/cardinality/chain conditions. In particular, empty
observation history cannot convert a bundle into a standalone archive.
Publication constructs an entirely separate normal profile; changing a marker
or renaming a table never constitutes publication.

## Required pre-implementation review

Review the event state machine, all cross-file crash outcomes and the ability to
resume or record failure without rewriting history. Freeze actual DDL, canonical
positive/re-signed-negative vectors and an independent Python encoder/verifier
before storage mutations are implemented. Pin M1 and R1 against independently
constructed empty, staged, missing, corrupt, restored and partial-copy fixtures.
Whole-output verification must include ordinary writable schema, original writer
signatures, issuer proof chain and profile-3 completion; M1 alone proves none of
those properties. The observer can report evidence, but cannot grant admission,
erase historical loss or assert a fabricated complete source-copy recipe.

### Publication state and replay rules

An attempt ID has exactly one intent. It may have zero or more failed observations
and at most one observed publication. A failure is evidence of an unsuccessful
check, not a terminal assertion that no valid output exists. Explicit resume may
therefore append observed after failure when it verifies that same attempt's
selected commitment and owner-specified output. No failed or second observed
record may follow observed for that attempt. A changed selection or different
output identity requires a new attempt ID and intent. Independent verifiers must
validate these relationships from the complete observation chain, not a mutable
status column.

Creation's single publication transaction includes a created event plus enough
unavailable events to cover every unavailable expected occurrence, every
missing/corrupt original-membership key (including unreferenced staged objects),
and every corrupt retained orphan row. Missing orphans with no surviving expected
coordinate cannot be invented. Exact repeated restoration is idempotent: return
the prior candidate/observation, without a new row or signature. A candidate
insert without its observation, or observation without its candidate, refuses.

The owner-selected observation frontier is an external checkpoint, comprising
sequence and statement CID under the full bundle/observer binding. Verifiers
must prove that checkpoint belongs to the observed chain and distinguish it from
any later verified extension. A file cannot supply its own rollback-detection
checkpoint. No cross-copy anti-equivocation beyond the explicitly pinned chain
is claimed.

### Checkpoints and multiple completed outputs

Several attempt IDs may each reach publication-observed. Each creates a separate
physical standalone output with the member's logical archive identity; none
activates a service. The owner must select exactly one live writer and fence the
others through the separately authorized activation workflow. The bundle cannot
promise that privileged manual configuration obeyed that workflow.

Every successful mutation/job result returns the verified observation frontier
(sequence plus statement CID and full binding), including a committed failure
observation. The owner verifies and durably retains it outside the bundle before
advancing the recovery UI's independently checkpointed status. On restart the
owner supplies the latest retained checkpoint; valid extensions are reported
separately until retained. A tail truncated after the latest external checkpoint
is not detectable. The online observer key can attribute new statements but does
not itself provide an independent tamper-evidence or non-equivocation witness.
An uncertain response may require explicit inspection and checkpoint advancement;
do not derive the external pin from the bundle being verified.

### Scope-C follow-through before format acceptance

The governing bundle design's "custody and owner-visible limits" section is part
of this codec contract: pre-open path checks cover all participating databases;
partial-copy restart provenance is external job state only; forensic-only source
cells are a named recovery gap; unrecoverable staged/orphan keys explicitly block
publication. None changes the byte recipes or adds a silently unsigned field to
the closed observation schema. Draft SQL and wire fixtures still require their
own independent review before acceptance or any storage writer.

## First implementation checkpoint: observation authentication

`src/evidence_recovery_observation.rs` implements only bounded canonical wire
validation, static P-256 owner pins, observer signature attribution and contiguous
observation predecessor links. `Authenticated` has private construction and
carries no bundle-completeness, member-truth or publication-state authority.
`sign_claim` is a pure signer and round-trip validator; its caller must establish
the permitted operation and semantic truth before using it. There is no storage
consumer, mutation, file routing, checkpoint acceptance or browser API here.

Independent Python fixtures exercise the six event forms, exact statement/CID/
signature bytes, maximum wire shapes and re-signed hostile cases. Their member,
restoration and output digest values deliberately do not establish a valid full
bundle. A wire-valid claim may still be false; complete bundle verification must
reject those false claims. The Rust API does not provide JSON serialization or
accept a caller-constructed predecessor as authenticated history.

The accompanying SQL fixture is a **draft** local-constraint schema, exercised
in memory with no publication markers. The M1/O1/R1 Python oracle is a **draft**
framing oracle, not a signed-record or complete-member verifier; synthetic record
bytes in its framing cases do not qualify any archive. Neither draft is accepted
as a storage compatibility promise by this checkpoint. Before a bundle writer:
implement and independently qualify streaming commitment computation, complete
member/proof validation, exact loss partitioning, candidate/history consistency,
publication replay and external-checkpoint validation; then freeze their complete
cross-implementation vectors and DDL. All recovery writer/job/RPC/UI criteria stay
open until their real operations and crash outcomes are tested and reviewed.

### Second independent review decisions

Observer authority is a separate role and signature domain from archive issuer
authority. The wire codec permits explicitly pinned equal observer/issuer DIDs;
it never treats an observer signature as an archive proof. Distinct-key policy
belongs to owner configuration. Recovery job configuration should default to a
separate observer key and disclose explicit reuse; equality in the wire is not
proof of independent authorities or compromise isolation. This interpretation
of parent REQ-1 is recorded rather than silently requiring a new wire restriction.
The same-key role fixture pins this decision.

Refusal reason strings in the cross-implementation fixtures identify their
single-fault cases. They do not define a total precedence for inputs with several
independent faults: Rust and Python may name different first faults while both
refuse. No authorization or state transition may depend on which diagnostic
string wins. Acceptance and byte identity remain the interoperability contract.

The expanded fixtures now distinguish canonical CID text order from binary order
for unavailable entries, original membership, original objects and R1 candidates.
The draft DDL bounds identifier text by bytes, excludes embedded NUL and requires
printable ASCII; complete canonical DID/CID validation remains a verifier duty.
SQLite's lossless affinity coercion is not a promise about caller bind types:
writers must bind typed values and readers must still check stored types.

An authenticated expected object length above 4 MiB also refuses KNB1 creation
as `forensic-recovery-required`, even when no oversized physical row survives.
Do not truncate the expected length or drop that reference to fit the format.
Retain source and failed output; the generic manifest schema's larger integer
range does not widen this proposed recovery format's representable object size.

## Next checkpoint draft: bounded streaming framing

The draft `evidence_recovery_commitment` module computes M1/O1/R1 incrementally.
Its caller supplies section counts and strictly increasing canonical CID-text
order; it does not allocate an archive-sized sort or payload buffer. Separate
membership/record/object stages enforce counts and contiguous record positions.
Any rejected builder operation poisons the builder, so ignoring an error cannot
produce a digest over fewer records. Empty corrupt originals remain representable;
restoration candidates must be nonempty and match their raw CID.

Owner-selected item, work-byte, time and cancellation limits bound computation;
hashing polls at most every 64 KiB. Work-byte accounting includes framing and,
for restoration, both candidate verification and commitment hashing. It does not
bound prior caller acquisition or arbitrary filesystem stalls. The caller remains
responsible for authorized bounded source reads and complete member semantics.
DID/record/plan truth, candidate membership and full state replay are not supplied
by these framing digests. This draft has no storage consumer. Author qualification passes eight commitment
tests against independent Python vectors and nine compiled controls, with strict
v2 Clippy and formatting. Evidence is in
`.design/reviews/kan-v2-recovery-commitment-author/`. Fresh independent review
remains pending; full member and state verification are separate prerequisites.


### Streaming review follow-through

Actual Opus 5.5 review of a8927a6 found no production defect and returned
APPROVE WITH FOLLOW-UPS; full raw evidence is retained in
`.design/reviews/kan-v2-recovery-commitment-opus/`. RA3/RA4 section/count/size
probes are promoted. Test-only cancellation injection qualifies polling within
hashing without timing sleeps; the original independent timing probe and its
recorded limits remain preserved. These follow-through tests pass author qualification: ten integration functions,
two deterministic polling units and thirteen compiled controls, plus strict
Clippy/format and the independent oracle. Evidence is in
`.design/reviews/kan-v2-recovery-commitment-followups-author/`. Fresh review with
the member-verifier checkpoint remains required.

The 1..80-byte framing issuer bound is explicit above and now shared by the
Python oracle. UTF-8 is pinned for future physical creation and opening. An O1
digest from the framing builder alone still authenticates no output bytes:
full object/writer/profile verification must precede publication. None of these
changes accepts the physical format or closes parent acceptance criteria.

## Next verifier checkpoint: logical member and initial availability

The pure member verifier takes an owner-pinned context and borrowed, ordered
record, membership and original-object slices. Its caller must acquire those
bytes with bounded reads before calling; this is not a SQLite opener. The physical
reader must reject noncanonical original CID text before constructing typed CIDs;
parsing a spelling and silently normalizing it is not source validation. Explicit
item/input-byte/time/cancellation limits bound this invocation. It stores only
bounded metadata coordinates, never copies the whole payload collection. Hashing
polls per 64 KiB; canonical decoding, request verification and signatures are
individually bounded operations with cancellation checks around them.

Independently verify the contiguous issuer chain, admitted versus retained-copy
purpose, static service writer form, per-writer position/predecessor, unique
operation, the service operation-to-slot commitment and consistent slot bindings. Profile 3 additionally binds its plan,
original membership and retained-prefix metadata digest. An unfinished prefix is
reported as incomplete; matching metadata alone does not certify missing writer
signatures or retained bytes. No standalone publication capability is returned.

Every known length must be positive, at most 4 MiB, and agree across references
and original membership. Retain raw corrupt/empty originals in M1. Verify each
present object's hash once and sample every occurrence separately; unreferenced
membership/original keys receive null-occurrence loss coordinates. A hash-valid
request that fails its writer signature or exact manifest binding is invalid
member evidence, not a repairable missing-byte condition. Missing/corrupt requests
remain unavailable, with writer verification still outstanding. Loss output is
strict occurrence/CID-text order, followed by null coordinates in CID-text order.

This checkpoint must be qualified before it can feed full observation replay.
Greedy signed-loss partitioning, historical restoration/output selection, replay,
checkpoints, physical schema and all storage mutations remain separate work.


The logical-member draft passes author qualification: 16 Rust functions,
independent signed Python fixtures, eight semantic controls (one additional
cancellation control survives because framing refuses later), strict Clippy and
formatting. Raw results are in
`.design/reviews/kan-v2-recovery-member-author/`. Fresh independent review is
pending; this is not full bundle acceptance.

1	# Feature: retained recovery bundles and explicit complete-output publication
2	
3	## Summary
4	A recovery bundle preserves a damaged physical copy, its exact authenticated
5	metadata, bounded retained ciphertext and an append-only record of loss and
6	recovery observations. It does not become capture-ready when a blob is restored.
7	This proposal resolves the physical-format/publication question C-F2 left open in
8	`kan-v2-evidence-availability.md`. It requires independent design review before a
9	bundle writer is implemented. The owner-copy storage PR does not implement it.
10	
11	## Requirements
12	- REQ-1: A bundle has its own owner-pinned copy identity and observer authority, separate from the logical archive/profile/issuer. Ordinary standalone profile-2/3 APIs must refuse the entire bundle, including after every missing payload has been restored.
13	- REQ-2: Preserve exact canonical manifests, receipts, issuer proofs, profile-3 plan and original-object membership. Preserve every copied bounded object byte even when corrupt; do not turn missing payloads into empty objects or re-sign issuer proofs.
14	- REQ-3: Append bounded canonical observer-signed creation, unavailable-evidence, restoration and publication observations. Verify sequence/predecessor, observer, bundle identity and configured observation frontier before trusting the history. Retain loss observations after resolution.
15	- REQ-4: Restoring bytes appends a separately identified verified candidate without overwriting the original corrupt or missing member. A bundle remains a recovery artifact. Only explicit owner resolution can create a separate fully verified standalone output.
16	- REQ-5: Publication retains the bundle and any failed output, verifies exact output profile/authority/payloads, records what was durably observed, and never auto-activates a writer. An uncertain crash or failed publication must not be reported as completed recovery.
17	- REQ-6: Bundle-aware backup/rebuild preserves both member evidence and the entire observation/restoration history. Standalone backup/rebuild is never an implicit fallback for a missing bundle ledger.
18	- REQ-7: Declare all file, schema, observation and restoration surfaces; enforce bounded materialization and owner-configured work/disk budgets. No plaintext content, fetched external resources, implicit erasure, or guessed repairs.
19	- REQ-8: Qualify envelope bytes with an independent implementation, all publication crash windows, missing-ledger/standalone escapes, source invariance and exact retained history; obtain fresh Opus approval before accepting a bundle implementation.
20	
21	## Acceptance Criteria
22	- [ ] AC-1: A bundle containing a complete backfilled logical profile 2 or 3 still refuses standalone open/admission/backup/rebuild. Missing or replaced observer history refuses bundle open rather than selecting standalone mode. (REQ-1, REQ-3, REQ-6)
23	- [ ] AC-2: Canonical positive and re-signed negative observation fixtures pin field sets, domain/preimage, signatures, identities, predecessor and source/output commitments in an independent implementation. (REQ-2, REQ-3, REQ-8)
24	- [ ] AC-3: Missing, corrupt and restored candidates retain distinct original evidence and observations; byte-identical issuer proofs and plans survive bundle backup/rebuild and successful output publication. (REQ-2, REQ-4, REQ-6)
25	- [ ] AC-4: Process death at every creation/restoration/publication boundary leaves a refused incomplete artifact, a valid retained bundle, or an independently verifiable complete output with honest pending/observed history. No automatic activation or false completed result occurs. (REQ-1, REQ-3, REQ-4, REQ-5, REQ-8)
26	- [ ] AC-5: Wrong external pins, path/sidecar collisions, stale source, unauthorized observer, oversized values, work-budget exhaustion and bad restored bytes refuse without rewriting original source/member evidence. (REQ-1, REQ-2, REQ-5, REQ-7)
27	- [ ] AC-6: Fresh review distinguishes logical recovery from physical publication, preserves failed probes, and demonstrates compiled controls for ledger omission, history overwrite, early completion and profile downgrade. (REQ-3, REQ-5, REQ-6, REQ-8)
28	
29	## Architecture
30	
31	The provenance and non-destructive projection constraints originate in
32	`docs/SPEC.md`; the v2 profile contracts below specialize its immutable-evidence
33	principle without treating disposable query state as authoritative records.
34	
35	Preserve the append-only evidence and provenance rules in `CLAUDE.md`. The
36	existing standalone lifecycle is in `src/evidence_store.rs`,
37	`src/evidence_store/attested.rs` and `src/evidence_store/copied.rs`; the proposed
38	bundle boundary must not call those openers as a fallback. Canonical service
39	proofs in `src/evidence_attestation.rs` remain unchanged, while the new observer
40	codec uses a separate domain. `tests/evidence_attested_lifecycle.rs` supplies the
41	existing crash/byte-preservation test patterns; bundle-specific tests remain to
42	be implemented after design approval.
43	
44	### Encapsulated logical member
45	
46	Propose a separate SQLite application ID `0x4b4e4231` (KNB1), user_version 1.
47	This is the physical **bundle** profile. Its member's logical profile remains 2
48	or 3, recorded explicitly in bundle identity; the member is not a nested
49	standalone SQLite file that an ordinary path configuration could open directly.
50	Existing archive application/profile markers never match the bundle. No product
51	option strips the bundle marker or treats absent observation tables as legacy.
52	Privileged manual extraction is outside this boundary and is not claimed prevented.
53	
54	The namespace contains:
55	
56	| Table | Authority and role |
57	| --- | --- |
58	| `bundle_identity` | singleton: bundle ID, observer DID, member logical profile and original archive/scope/issuer pins; commitment/frontier live in the signed created event |
59	| `member_objects` | exact original object keys and bounded bytes, including corrupt bytes; absent rows remain absent |
60	| `member_records` | exact manifest/receipt/proof bytes together by occurrence sequence; never newly issued |
61	| `member_plan` | exact canonical profile-3 plan, absent for profile 2 |
62	| `member_membership` | exact original membership and lengths, absent for profile 2 |
63	| `observations` | contiguous observer-signed canonical envelopes; append only |
64	| `restored_objects` | append-only verified candidates by expected content address, with no updates to member_objects |
65	
66	All SQL column definitions, constraints, indexes and typed mutations must be
67	frozen alongside the codec before writing. This table is the design inventory,
68	not a claim that the physical schema already exists. There is no independently
69	writable standalone archive member. Normal bundle queries preserve the distinction
70	between original evidence and restored candidates.
71	
72	Creation requires a stopped/pinned source and a fully verified metadata chain.
73	Original payload bytes are copied even if they fail their expected hash or length,
74	provided they fit the protocol's bounded materialization limit. Unknown schemas,
75	invalid object keys or oversized corrupt cells refuse this first format; original
76	media stays retained for a separate forensic workflow. No arbitrary SQLite repair
77	or implicit omission is claimed. A missing row contributes a loss observation,
78	never a fabricated object. Staged objects are included in owner recovery inventory,
79	but are not exposed as authorized browser occurrences without metadata membership.
80	
81	### Canonical observation protocol proposal
82	
83	The codec appendix is the single proposed wire definition. Use its flat canonical
84	DAG-CBOR statement with `version`, `domain`, full pinned context, sequence,
85	previous, `sampledAt`, `event` and event-specific `body`, inside the closed
86	`{statement:<exact bytes>,signature:<64 low-S P-256 bytes>}` envelope, max 16 KiB.
87	There is no alternative `v/kind/body` statement wrapper.
88	Signature preimage is canonical `{domain:"tools.kan.recovery.observation.v1",
89	statement:<statement CID>}`. Require canonical static observer DID/method and
90	safe-integer sequence/time. No reuse of service admission signature domains.
91	
92	Every statement commits to bundle ID, logical archive ID/profile/scope/issuer, observer,
93	positive sequence, previous statement CID (null only at sequence 1), sampled-at
94	milliseconds, event kind and a closed event-specific payload. Event variants:
95	
96	- `created`: initial member commitment, source metadata frontier, chosen recipe 1.
97	- `unavailable`: bounded references with occurrence sequence (or explicit staged
98	  object designation), expected CID/length and sampled missing/corrupt state.
99	- `restored`: expected CID/length and verified candidate commitment; this reports
100	  a checked restoration candidate, not activation or completed archive recovery.
101	- `publication-intent`: selected member/restoration commitments, target logical
102	  profile/frontier and owner-selected output attempt ID; no success assertion.
103	- `publication-observed`: cites that intent and exact verified durable output
104	  commitment/frontier. It records the observer's completed publication check.
105	- `publication-failed`: cites intent and bounded failure class, without erasing it
106	  or certifying that no output exists.
107	
108	References and encoded size are both bounded; long inventories use multiple
109	linked records. Timestamps do not establish order. Observer O may be provisioned
110	on the same host as issuer C but has a distinct declared authority/domain. O's
111	signature never replaces C's admission proof or a writer's original signature.
112	Source and output paths are owner-local routing inputs, not trusted executable
113	instructions from signed observations. No shell command is stored or executed.
114	
115	The initial member commitment needs a frozen domain/byte-framing recipe over
116	logical identity/profile, exact plan or explicit absence, canonical original
117	membership, exact records/proofs in sequence, and all original object key/length/
118	raw-byte commitments in canonical key order. Unlike a normal object CID check,
119	it must commit to corrupt retained bytes as observed. Independent fixtures must
120	cover empty/missing/corrupt/staged cases and profile-3 partial copies. The full
121	byte recipe is a required codec checkpoint, not an implementer's implicit choice.
122	
123	### Creation and restoration transactions
124	
125	Create a new private outer database without a recognized bundle marker. A bounded
126	owner job copies and verifies member metadata, retains bounded original objects,
127	and inserts creation/loss observations. Publish the bundle marker only in the
128	same successful transaction as the complete initial member and initial history;
129	fsync the file and parent before reporting success. A failed/oversized job retains
130	an unrecognized output and source. Non-BLOB source object cells refuse creation rather than being cast to bytes.
131	Work budgets are explicit instance/owner
132	resource limits, not a new fixed repository-size ceiling disguised as a protocol
133	limit. A resumable multi-transaction creator needs a separate pinned-plan design;
134	it must not label a partially copied bundle complete.
135	
136	Restoration validates a candidate's expected CID/length and its membership before
137	atomically inserting it and an observation. Original member rows and prior loss
138	observations never change. Repeating exact verified bytes is idempotent and does
139	not invent new issuer provenance. A different candidate for the same CID refuses.
140	The bundle's inventory may show a verified restoration candidate alongside the
141	original missing/corrupt state; it never silently substitutes history.
142	
143	### Resolution and publication
144	
145	The owner selects a new output path and exact bundle/history frontier. Verify all
146	chosen payloads, current writer signatures, issuer proofs, original plan/membership
147	and structural constraints. A partial profile-3 member is retained and inspectable but is ineligible for
148	standalone publication in KNB1. Its immutable member cannot gain missing metadata
149	through blob restoration. The owner can use the existing source-copy workflow
150	on a separately retained complete original source, first confirming that source
151	against the old pinned plan/digest, to create a different verified output using a new nonce and hence a new archive ID; retain the old bundle and
152	its entire observation history, with the owner job recording the original bundle
153	ID/checkpoint as a provenance reference. That is not publication from this partial
154	bundle and must not be reported
155	as such. Completing a partial member inside its bundle would require a separately
156	reviewed append-only metadata-extension protocol, which KNB1 does not provide.
157	This limitation is visible in the job/UI capability result, not a repair guess.
158	
159	Publication deterministically selects the candidate set recorded before its
160	intent, as specified by R1 in the codec appendix. Later restorations require a
161	new attempt and cannot silently alter an old selection.
162	
163	Append `publication-intent` before creating an output. Build a new standalone
164	file using exact original metadata/proofs/plan and verified selected payloads,
165	rebuilding only derived columns. Keep it unrecognized until full verification
166	succeeds inside its publication transaction, as the existing rebuild API does.
167	Durably publish and re-verify the result, then append `publication-observed` and
168	return a completed job result. Do not automatically switch the service target.
169	The owner must separately fence the old writer and activate one selected output.
170	
171	SQLite cannot atomically commit an external file and the bundle observation
172	ledger. Therefore a crash can leave a fully verified standalone output with an
173	unresolved intent. This is **uncertain publication**, not completed recovery. The
174	next explicit resume verifies that exact output and appends the observed outcome,
175	or records failure and retains all artifacts. It never guesses completion from a
176	filename or overwrites a different existing output. A completed physical output
177	can be verified independently even when its acknowledgment was lost; no claim is
178	made that privileged early manual configuration is cryptographically impossible.
179	Ordinary job/administration flows activate only an explicitly selected completed
180	publication result, and never activate on a pending/failed intent.
181	
182	This distinction is a review point for C-F2: the encapsulated bundle cannot escape
183	as standalone, while a separate fully verified output may exist before its final
184	observation acknowledgment. The implementation must not conflate artifact validity,
185	observed publication, job success and live writer activation.
186
