# Feature: retained recovery bundles and explicit complete-output publication

## Summary
A recovery bundle preserves a damaged physical copy, its exact authenticated
metadata, bounded retained ciphertext and an append-only record of loss and
recovery observations. It does not become capture-ready when a blob is restored.
This proposal resolves the physical-format/publication question C-F2 left open in
`kan-v2-evidence-availability.md`. It requires independent design review before a
bundle writer is implemented. The owner-copy storage PR does not implement it.

## Requirements
- REQ-1: A bundle has its own owner-pinned copy identity and observer authority, separate from the logical archive/profile/issuer. Ordinary standalone profile-2/3 APIs must refuse the entire bundle, including after every missing payload has been restored.
- REQ-2: Preserve exact canonical manifests, receipts, issuer proofs, profile-3 plan and original-object membership. Preserve every copied bounded object byte even when corrupt; do not turn missing payloads into empty objects or re-sign issuer proofs.
- REQ-3: Append bounded canonical observer-signed creation, unavailable-evidence, restoration and publication observations. Verify sequence/predecessor, observer, bundle identity and configured observation frontier before trusting the history. Retain loss observations after resolution.
- REQ-4: Restoring bytes appends a separately identified verified candidate without overwriting the original corrupt or missing member. A bundle remains a recovery artifact. Only explicit owner resolution can create a separate fully verified standalone output.
- REQ-5: Publication retains the bundle and any failed output, verifies exact output profile/authority/payloads, records what was durably observed, and never auto-activates a writer. An uncertain crash or failed publication must not be reported as completed recovery.
- REQ-6: Bundle-aware backup/rebuild preserves both member evidence and the entire observation/restoration history. Standalone backup/rebuild is never an implicit fallback for a missing bundle ledger.
- REQ-7: Declare all file, schema, observation and restoration surfaces; enforce bounded materialization and owner-configured work/disk budgets. No plaintext content, fetched external resources, implicit erasure, or guessed repairs.
- REQ-8: Qualify envelope bytes with an independent implementation, all publication crash windows, missing-ledger/standalone escapes, source invariance and exact retained history; obtain fresh Opus approval before accepting a bundle implementation.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] AC-1: A bundle containing a complete backfilled logical profile 2 or 3 still refuses standalone open/admission/backup/rebuild. Missing or replaced observer history refuses bundle open rather than selecting standalone mode. (REQ-1, REQ-3, REQ-6)
- [ ] AC-2: Canonical positive and re-signed negative observation fixtures pin field sets, domain/preimage, signatures, identities, predecessor and source/output commitments in an independent implementation. (REQ-2, REQ-3, REQ-8)
- [ ] AC-3: Missing, corrupt and restored candidates retain distinct original evidence and observations; byte-identical issuer proofs and plans survive bundle backup/rebuild and successful output publication. (REQ-2, REQ-4, REQ-6)
- [ ] AC-4: Process death at every creation/restoration/publication boundary leaves a refused incomplete artifact, a valid retained bundle, or an independently verifiable complete output with honest pending/observed history. No automatic activation or false completed result occurs. (REQ-1, REQ-3, REQ-4, REQ-5, REQ-8)
- [ ] AC-5: Wrong external pins, path/sidecar collisions, stale source, unauthorized observer, oversized values, work-budget exhaustion and bad restored bytes refuse without rewriting original source/member evidence. (REQ-1, REQ-2, REQ-5, REQ-7)
- [ ] AC-6: Fresh review distinguishes logical recovery from physical publication, preserves failed probes, and demonstrates compiled controls for ledger omission, history overwrite, early completion and profile downgrade. (REQ-3, REQ-5, REQ-6, REQ-8)

## Architecture

The provenance and non-destructive projection constraints originate in
`docs/SPEC.md`; the v2 profile contracts below specialize its immutable-evidence
principle without treating disposable query state as authoritative records.

Preserve the append-only evidence and provenance rules in `CLAUDE.md`. The
existing standalone lifecycle is in `src/evidence_store.rs`,
`src/evidence_store/attested.rs` and `src/evidence_store/copied.rs`; the proposed
bundle boundary must not call those openers as a fallback. Canonical service
proofs in `src/evidence_attestation.rs` remain unchanged, while the new observer
codec uses a separate domain. `tests/evidence_attested_lifecycle.rs` supplies the
existing crash/byte-preservation test patterns; bundle-specific tests remain to
be implemented after design approval.

### Encapsulated logical member

Propose a separate SQLite application ID `0x4b4e4231` (KNB1), user_version 1.
This is the physical **bundle** profile. Its member's logical profile remains 2
or 3, recorded explicitly in bundle identity; the member is not a nested
standalone SQLite file that an ordinary path configuration could open directly.
Existing archive application/profile markers never match the bundle. No product
option strips the bundle marker or treats absent observation tables as legacy.
Privileged manual extraction is outside this boundary and is not claimed prevented.

The namespace contains:

| Table | Authority and role |
| --- | --- |
| `bundle_identity` | singleton: bundle ID, observer DID, member logical profile and original archive/scope/issuer pins; commitment/frontier live in the signed created event |
| `member_objects` | exact original object keys and bounded bytes, including corrupt bytes; absent rows remain absent |
| `member_records` | exact manifest/receipt/proof bytes together by occurrence sequence; never newly issued |
| `member_plan` | exact canonical profile-3 plan, absent for profile 2 |
| `member_membership` | exact original membership and lengths, absent for profile 2 |
| `observations` | contiguous observer-signed canonical envelopes; append only |
| `restored_objects` | append-only verified candidates by expected content address, with no updates to member_objects |

All SQL column definitions, constraints, indexes and typed mutations must be
frozen alongside the codec before writing. This table is the design inventory,
not a claim that the physical schema already exists. There is no independently
writable standalone archive member. Normal bundle queries preserve the distinction
between original evidence and restored candidates.

Creation requires a stopped/pinned source and a fully verified metadata chain.
Original payload bytes are copied even if they fail their expected hash or length,
provided they fit the protocol's bounded materialization limit. Unknown schemas,
invalid object keys or oversized corrupt cells refuse this first format; original
media stays retained for a separate forensic workflow. No arbitrary SQLite repair
or implicit omission is claimed. A missing row contributes a loss observation,
never a fabricated object. Staged objects are included in owner recovery inventory,
but are not exposed as authorized browser occurrences without metadata membership.

### Canonical observation protocol proposal

The codec appendix is the single proposed wire definition. Use its flat canonical
DAG-CBOR statement with `version`, `domain`, full pinned context, sequence,
previous, `sampledAt`, `event` and event-specific `body`, inside the closed
`{statement:<exact bytes>,signature:<64 low-S P-256 bytes>}` envelope, max 16 KiB.
There is no alternative `v/kind/body` statement wrapper.
Signature preimage is canonical `{domain:"tools.kan.recovery.observation.v1",
statement:<statement CID>}`. Require canonical static observer DID/method and
safe-integer sequence/time. No reuse of service admission signature domains.

Every statement commits to bundle ID, logical archive ID/profile/scope/issuer, observer,
positive sequence, previous statement CID (null only at sequence 1), sampled-at
milliseconds, event kind and a closed event-specific payload. Event variants:

- `created`: initial member commitment, source metadata frontier, chosen recipe 1.
- `unavailable`: bounded references with occurrence sequence (or explicit staged
  object designation), expected CID/length and sampled missing/corrupt state.
- `restored`: expected CID/length and verified candidate commitment; this reports
  a checked restoration candidate, not activation or completed archive recovery.
- `publication-intent`: selected member/restoration commitments, target logical
  profile/frontier and owner-selected output attempt ID; no success assertion.
- `publication-observed`: cites that intent and exact verified durable output
  commitment/frontier. It records the observer's completed publication check.
- `publication-failed`: cites intent and bounded failure class, without erasing it
  or certifying that no output exists.

References and encoded size are both bounded; long inventories use multiple
linked records. Timestamps do not establish order. Observer O may be provisioned
on the same host as issuer C but has a distinct declared authority/domain. O's
signature never replaces C's admission proof or a writer's original signature.
Source and output paths are owner-local routing inputs, not trusted executable
instructions from signed observations. No shell command is stored or executed.

The initial member commitment needs a frozen domain/byte-framing recipe over
logical identity/profile, exact plan or explicit absence, canonical original
membership, exact records/proofs in sequence, and all original object key/length/
raw-byte commitments in canonical key order. Unlike a normal object CID check,
it must commit to corrupt retained bytes as observed. Independent fixtures must
cover empty/missing/corrupt/staged cases and profile-3 partial copies. The full
byte recipe is a required codec checkpoint, not an implementer's implicit choice.

### Creation and restoration transactions

Create a new private outer database without a recognized bundle marker. A bounded
owner job copies and verifies member metadata, retains bounded original objects,
and inserts creation/loss observations. Publish the bundle marker only in the
same successful transaction as the complete initial member and initial history;
fsync the file and parent before reporting success. A failed/oversized job retains
an unrecognized output and source. Non-BLOB source object cells refuse creation rather than being cast to bytes.
Work budgets are explicit instance/owner
resource limits, not a new fixed repository-size ceiling disguised as a protocol
limit. A resumable multi-transaction creator needs a separate pinned-plan design;
it must not label a partially copied bundle complete.

Restoration validates a candidate's expected CID/length and its membership before
atomically inserting it and an observation. Original member rows and prior loss
observations never change. Repeating exact verified bytes is idempotent and does
not invent new issuer provenance. A different candidate for the same CID refuses.
The bundle's inventory may show a verified restoration candidate alongside the
original missing/corrupt state; it never silently substitutes history.

### Resolution and publication

The owner selects a new output path and exact bundle/history frontier. Verify all
chosen payloads, current writer signatures, issuer proofs, original plan/membership
and structural constraints. A partial profile-3 member is retained and inspectable but is ineligible for
standalone publication in KNB1. Its immutable member cannot gain missing metadata
through blob restoration. The owner can use the existing source-copy workflow
on a separately retained complete original source, first confirming that source
against the old pinned plan/digest, to create a different verified output using a new nonce and hence a new archive ID; retain the old bundle and
its entire observation history, with the owner job recording the original bundle
ID/checkpoint as a provenance reference. That is not publication from this partial
bundle and must not be reported
as such. Completing a partial member inside its bundle would require a separately
reviewed append-only metadata-extension protocol, which KNB1 does not provide.
This limitation is visible in the job/UI capability result, not a repair guess.

Publication deterministically selects the candidate set recorded before its
intent, as specified by R1 in the codec appendix. Later restorations require a
new attempt and cannot silently alter an old selection.

Append `publication-intent` before creating an output. Build a new standalone
file using exact original metadata/proofs/plan and verified selected payloads,
rebuilding only derived columns. Keep it unrecognized until full verification
succeeds inside its publication transaction, as the existing rebuild API does.
Durably publish and re-verify the result, then append `publication-observed` and
return a completed job result. Do not automatically switch the service target.
The owner must separately fence the old writer and activate one selected output.

SQLite cannot atomically commit an external file and the bundle observation
ledger. Therefore a crash can leave a fully verified standalone output with an
unresolved intent. This is **uncertain publication**, not completed recovery. The
next explicit resume verifies that exact output and appends the observed outcome,
or records failure and retains all artifacts. It never guesses completion from a
filename or overwrites a different existing output. A completed physical output
can be verified independently even when its acknowledgment was lost; no claim is
made that privileged early manual configuration is cryptographically impossible.
Ordinary job/administration flows activate only an explicitly selected completed
publication result, and never activate on a pending/failed intent.

This distinction is a review point for C-F2: the encapsulated bundle cannot escape
as standalone, while a separate fully verified output may exist before its final
observation acknowledgment. The implementation must not conflate artifact validity,
observed publication, job success and live writer activation.

### Backup, rebuild and grants

A bundle backup is a consistent snapshot of the entire outer database, verified
against owner pins and the selected observation frontier. A bundle rebuild copies
all authoritative member/restoration/observation bytes into a new outer profile
and rebuilds disposable indexes. Missing member payloads remain missing; missing
observation history is a hard integrity failure. No fallback to standalone file
commands or omission of unresolved attempts is allowed.

Bundle IDs name physical recovery copies, not new logical archives. A backup
preserves the bundle identity and history; two copies can have different future
observations. Owner configuration must select a single observation writer or
explicitly provision a new bundle identity for an independent observation branch.
No cross-host anti-equivocation or silent merge of observer histories is claimed.
Browser scope access remains governed by the same current grants as inventory;
owner recovery and publication require separate administrative capabilities.

## Proposed codec checkpoint

`kan-v2-recovery-bundle-codec.md` now specifies the proposed observation schema,
domain-separated signature preimage, M1/R1 byte framing, member table shapes and
publication replay rules. It remains a proposal pending independent review and
independent byte fixtures; no bundle writer exists.

## Open qualification work

Freeze the complete body field names, member commitment framing, observation
reference bounds and physical SQL definitions in a dedicated codec patch. Produce
independent positive/re-signed-negative fixtures and obtain fresh Opus review of
C-F2 before any writer exists. Then implement storage, crash tests and owner job
APIs; only afterward integrate the human recovery workflow. These are required
remaining steps, not completion claims or a reduction of the full frontend scope.

## Design review follow-through: custody and owner-visible limits

Before any SQLite open of a source, bundle or publication output, each operation
must perform the filesystem-only path custody checks for every proposed output
against every participating SQLite file and its reserved sidecar namespace.
Recheck at creation/retention as well. This carries the copy-plan pre-open lesson
into creation, restoration and publication; it does not claim a hostile
namespace-replacement fence or qualification on untested filesystems.

The partial-copy restart reference lives **only in external owner job records**
under the later job schema: old bundle ID, pinned observation checkpoint, old
plan identity and the new copy plan/output identity. KNB1 and copy-plan v1 do not
contain a restart/superseded event or provenance field. Neither file's signed
history may be presented as asserting that relationship. Until the external job
record contract is implemented and reviewed, the UI cannot report a provenance-
linked restart as a completed capability.

Two distinct owner-visible recovery limits remain named roadmap work:

- `forensic-recovery-required`: non-BLOB, malformed-key, unreadable or oversized
  original cells cannot be encoded in KNB1. Inventory may still browse healthy
  neighbours and report corruption, but the recovery job must retain the source
  and failed output, disclose this refusal, and offer no successful bundle claim.
  A forensic preservation/recovery format and workflow remain unimplemented.
- `publication-blocked-unavailable-object`: any required key without verified
  original or restoration bytes blocks KNB1 publication, including a never-
  admitted staged/orphan object. If no bytes can be recovered, this is terminal
  for that proposed publication under KNB1; retain the bundle and expose the key
  and its original loss state. Later verified recovery may allow a new attempt.
  No discard-orphan escape hatch or automatic erasure is implied.

These are proposed capability/refusal labels, not implemented RPC enum values.
They complement the already explicit partial-profile-3 limitation. The storage
writer, owner jobs and full human frontend must implement and test them before
claiming recovery coverage.

The second codec review clarifies that REQ-1 separates observer and issuer roles
and signature domains; equal explicitly pinned keys are wire-valid but do not
provide independent-key isolation. Owner recovery jobs default to distinct keys
and disclose reuse. The codec appendix records this decision and diagnostic
precedence limits. `forensic-recovery-required` also covers authenticated expected
object lengths beyond 4 MiB, whether or not the original object row is present.

# Logical member verifier: author qualification

Sixteen Rust test functions pass, including real writer requests in both profiles,
empty and complete members, an admitted suffix after a copied prefix, partial
copy status, exact occurrence/orphan losses, conflicting lengths, issuer-resigned
false copy digests, missing membership, writer predecessor/operation/slot checks,
hash-valid invalid writer signatures and exact manifest substitution. Limits
cover item/input-byte caps, initial cancellation, a tiny elapsed-time allowance
and oversized physical/expected lengths. Strict v2 all-target Clippy and format
pass.

The independent Python generator constructs 16 cases (7 positive, 9 hostile),
with real canonical signed requests, receipts and P-256 issuer proofs, using
only public test scalars. Its separate attestation verifier checks constructed
chains; its M1 and loss oracle match Rust. It is explicitly not a complete second
member-semantic verifier. The byte-identical fixtures regenerate and check.

Eight compiled guard removals fail named assertions: item/input budgets, source
digest, expected-length agreement, duplicate operations, original payload hash,
orphan loss preservation and invocation of retained-writer verification.
Restored tests pass. The early cancellation guard mutation SURVIVES: later
commitment framing still refuses cancellation. This does not cover prompt
interruption of earlier metadata/hash work. The initial runner stopped on that
survivor; its raw failure is retained alongside the final run with the survivor
explicitly reported, rather than relabelled as a kill.

This is pure verification of caller-acquired bounded inputs. Original corrupt
bytes are retained in M1. A missing/corrupt request is not a verified writer
request. The result grants no observation-history, physical-format, publication
or durability authority. Full loss-event partitioning, restoration/output/state
replay, checkpoints, schema reads, writer/crash jobs, RPC and UI remain required.
Fresh actual Opus 5.5 review is pending. No production archive/key was read.


After merging the framing audit/follow-through (99f1fba), the combined baseline
passes 33 integration functions (16 member, 8 commitment, 2 promoted commitment,
7 observation) and two deterministic polling units. Strict all-target v2 Clippy,
format and the independent member fixture regeneration check pass. The merge
keeps both additive CI targets and design sections. No runtime changes were made
by conflict resolution. The combined source is ready for independent review.

# Logical member verifier: author qualification

Sixteen Rust test functions pass, including real writer requests in both profiles,
empty and complete members, an admitted suffix after a copied prefix, partial
copy status, exact occurrence/orphan losses, conflicting lengths, issuer-resigned
false copy digests, missing membership, writer predecessor/operation/slot checks,
hash-valid invalid writer signatures and exact manifest substitution. Limits
cover item/input-byte caps, initial cancellation, a tiny elapsed-time allowance
and oversized physical/expected lengths. Strict v2 all-target Clippy and format
pass.

The independent Python generator constructs 16 cases (7 positive, 9 hostile),
with real canonical signed requests, receipts and P-256 issuer proofs, using
only public test scalars. Its separate attestation verifier checks constructed
chains; its M1 and loss oracle match Rust. It is explicitly not a complete second
member-semantic verifier. The byte-identical fixtures regenerate and check.

Eight compiled guard removals fail named assertions: item/input budgets, source
digest, expected-length agreement, duplicate operations, original payload hash,
orphan loss preservation and invocation of retained-writer verification.
Restored tests pass. The early cancellation guard mutation SURVIVES: later
commitment framing still refuses cancellation. This does not cover prompt
interruption of earlier metadata/hash work. The initial runner stopped on that
survivor; its raw failure is retained alongside the final run with the survivor
explicitly reported, rather than relabelled as a kill.

This is pure verification of caller-acquired bounded inputs. Original corrupt
bytes are retained in M1. A missing/corrupt request is not a verified writer
request. The result grants no observation-history, physical-format, publication
or durability authority. Full loss-event partitioning, restoration/output/state
replay, checkpoints, schema reads, writer/crash jobs, RPC and UI remain required.
Fresh actual Opus 5.5 review is pending. No production archive/key was read.

def run_tests():

    t=time.time(); p=subprocess.run(cmd,cwd=EXPORT,capture_output=True,text=True,timeout=1800)

    failed = re.findall(r'^test (\S+) \.\.\. FAILED', log, re.M)
    panics = re.findall(r"panicked at ([^\n]+)\n([^\n]*)\n?([^\n]*)", log)
    compile_err = 'could not compile' in log or 'error[E' in log
    return failed, panics, compile_err
def main():
    os.makedirs(OUT, exist_ok=True)

    text = original.decode()
    which = sys.argv[1:] or [c[0] for c in AUTHOR+REVIEWER]
    summary=[]
    try:
        for name, old, new in AUTHOR+REVIEWER:
            if name not in which: continue
            n = text.count(old)
            if n != 1:

            open(FILE,'w').write(text.replace(old,new))
            rc, log, dt, cmd = run_tests()
            open(FILE,'wb').write(original)
            assert sha(FILE)==FROZEN, "restore failed"
            failed, panics, cerr = classify(log)
            with open(os.path.join(OUT,name+'.txt'),'w') as fh:
                fh.write(f"# mutation {name}\n# old: {old!r}\n# new: {new!r}\n# cmd: {' '.join(cmd)}\n# exit={rc} elapsed={dt:.1f}s restored_sha256={sha(FILE)}\n\n"+log)
            status = "COMPILE-ERROR" if cerr else ("SURVIVED" if rc==0 else "KILLED")
            line=f"{name}\t{status}\tfailed={','.join(failed) or '-'}"
            summary.append(line); print(line, flush=True)
    finally:
        open(FILE,'wb').write(original)
        assert sha(FILE)==FROZEN
    with open(os.path.join(OUT,'SUMMARY-'+time.strftime('%H%M%S')+'.tsv'),'w') as fh: fh.write("\n".join(summary)+"\n")
if __name__=='__main__': main()

 ('R18-record-position','require(row.sequence == frontier.through + 1, "record position")?;','require(true || row.sequence == frontier.through + 1, "record position")?;'),
]
def sha(p): return hashlib.sha256(open(p,'rb').read()).hexdigest()
def run_tests():
    cmd = ["cargo","test","--offline","--no-fail-fast","--features","v2-crypto","--test","evidence_recovery_member","--test","zz_review_member_probes","--","--test-threads=1"]
    t=time.time(); p=subprocess.run(cmd,cwd=EXPORT,capture_output=True,text=True,timeout=1800)
    return p.returncode, p.stdout+p.stderr, time.time()-t, cmd
def classify(log):
    failed = re.findall(r'^test (\S+) \.\.\. FAILED', log, re.M)
    panics = re.findall(r"panicked at ([^\n]+)\n([^\n]*)\n?([^\n]*)", log)
    compile_err = 'could not compile' in log or 'error[E' in log
    return failed, panics, compile_err
def main():
    os.makedirs(OUT, exist_ok=True)
    original = open(FILE,'rb').read()
    assert hashlib.sha256(original).hexdigest()==FROZEN, "source not frozen before controls"
    text = original.decode()
    which = sys.argv[1:] or [c[0] for c in AUTHOR+REVIEWER]
    summary=[]
    try:
        for name, old, new in AUTHOR+REVIEWER:
            if name not in which: continue
            n = text.count(old)
            if n != 1:
                summary.append(f"{name}\tNOT-APPLIED count={n}"); print(summary[-1], flush=True); continue
            open(FILE,'w').write(text.replace(old,new))
            rc, log, dt, cmd = run_tests()
            open(FILE,'wb').write(original)
            assert sha(FILE)==FROZEN, "restore failed"
            failed, panics, cerr = classify(log)
            with open(os.path.join(OUT,name+'.txt'),'w') as fh:
                fh.write(f"# mutation {name}\n# old: {old!r}\n# new: {new!r}\n# cmd: {' '.join(cmd)}\n# exit={rc} elapsed={dt:.1f}s restored_sha256={sha(FILE)}\n\n"+log)
            status = "COMPILE-ERROR" if cerr else ("SURVIVED" if rc==0 else "KILLED")
            line=f"{name}\t{status}\tfailed={','.join(failed) or '-'}"
            summary.append(line); print(line, flush=True)
    finally:
        open(FILE,'wb').write(original)
        assert sha(FILE)==FROZEN
    with open(os.path.join(OUT,'SUMMARY-'+time.strftime('%H%M%S')+'.tsv'),'w') as fh: fh.write("\n".join(summary)+"\n")
if __name__=='__main__': main()

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""For each mutation log, print per failing test: panic site and left/right/message lines."""
import os, re, sys
D = sys.argv[1]
for f in sorted(os.listdir(D)):
    if not f.endswith('.txt'): continue
    s = open(os.path.join(D, f)).read()
    print(f"=== {f[:-4]}")
    for m in re.finditer(r"thread '([^']+)' \(\d+\) panicked at ([^\n]+):\n((?:[^\n]*\n){1,4})", s):
        test, site, rest = m.groups()
        rest = " | ".join(l.strip() for l in rest.splitlines() if l.strip() and not l.startswith('note:') and not l.startswith('stack'))
        print(f"  {test} @ {site}\n      {rest[:400]}")
EOF

A. LOGICAL RECOVERY-MEMBER VERIFIER (src/evidence_recovery_member.rs, 552 lines; read in full)

Code facts used below:
- verify() takes an owner Context plus borrowed slices (:76-82). It has no fs/SQLite/rusqlite use; grep finds

- Framing receives the remaining duration and the shared cancel flag (:501-509).
- Per-writer chain (:355-364), unique (writer, op) (:366-369), single entry and slot == SHA-256(op)

- Source digest (:290-295, :398-407, :413-429) is byte-identical in recipe to src/evidence_store/copied.rs:148-198.
- Object validity = nonempty && known length matches && hash matches (:447-454).
- Writer verification runs only for Available occurrences (:461-473). Null coordinates cover unreferenced
  non-available keys (:483-493).
- Member has private fields and getters only (:98-125). It has no publication, history or durability surface.
- Manifest/receipt schemas are closed with all fields required (src/evidence.rs:463-522), so the Ipld
  indexing at :341-378 cannot hit a missing key.

Reviewer probes (probes/zz_review_member_probes.rs: 16 tests; probes/zz_review_member_probes2.rs: 4 tests).
On the unmodified tree all pass (logs/13, logs/14). Observations:
- RP01: an unreferenced staged membership key in a COMPLETE copy gets exactly one null coordinate with its
  authenticated length.
  - Missing gives missing; tampered gives corrupt.
  - Combined order is [occ1 corrupt, occ2 missing, null staged missing], as codec :168-170 requires.

  - Silently dropping a staged key is accepted.
  - Re-lengthening a staged key turns valid bytes into "corrupt".
  - The same fabrication in a complete copy refuses with "source metadata digest".
- RP03: two occurrences sharing one request CID are accepted, with bytes missing, as two "missing" losses.
  Supplying the genuine bytes then refuses with "retained writer request". No bytes can ever satisfy it.
- RP04: retained receipts from the current issuer instead of the plan's historical issuer refuse with
  "historical receipt issuer", with bytes present or missing.
- RP05: a plan tip at a non-final manifest, with a correct digest, refuses with "source tip".
- RP06: plan target scope or issuer differing from the owner context refuses with "plan binding". Archive
  equality alone is insufficient.
- RP07: admitted purpose inside the retained range refuses with "proof purpose". The mixed case refuses with
  "historical receipt issuer" first; the codec says diagnostic precedence is not contract.
- RP08: reversed, duplicate or DAG-CBOR membership refuses. Profile-2 membership refuses, as does profile 3
  without a plan.
- RP09: the record schema already refuses non-static did:key writers. For did:web+documentCid and
  did:plc+versionId writers with bytes missing, the verifier refuses with "static writer".
- RP10a: pre-cancelled with a later broken proof gives Cancelled.
- RP10b (timing): cancel at 20% of a 64 MiB member stage (~1.7 s) gives Cancelled after 0.3–1.1 ms.
- RP10c: a deadline of 342 ms returned Budget at 343.5 ms.
- RP10d (timing, finer): worst cancel latency over 6 offsets was 1.15 ms, against a 106 ms single 4 MiB hash.
- RP11: items=0, or input_bytes one below a 4 MiB object, gives Budget; the exact amount is accepted.
- RP12: wrong owner scope or issuer gives "issuer proof". A non-canonical observer gives "issuer encoding".
  A same-key observer is accepted, per the recorded decision.
- RP13: the DASL parser refuses uppercase CID text, so a typed Cid cannot carry a non-canonical spelling.
- RP14a (characterisation): the GENUINE hash-valid signed request bytes are present, but the
  issuer-re-signed manifest length is n+1. Result: the member is ACCEPTED, verified_requests=0 and the loss
  is {occ 1, expectedLength n+1, Corrupt}. See finding A-F1.
- RP14b: the empty-bytes CID referenced with signed length 1, with the empty row present, is accepted as
  Corrupt.
- RP15: an empty orphan keyed by the empty-bytes CID gives a null Corrupt loss.

- RP17: a broken writer chain with bytes missing refuses with "writer predecessor".

Compiled guard-removal controls (cmd/controls.py; mutations/*.txt; kill messages in logs/21 and logs/23).
- Reproduction of the author's 9:
  - 8 are killed with semantic assertions, i.e. Ok where a refusal was due, or a wrong loss vector:
    item-budget, input-budget, source-digest, expected-length, duplicate-operation, original-hash,
    orphan-loss, writer-signature.
  - A-expected-length: its kills in the owner_pins test and the conflicting-membership Python case are
    LABEL-ONLY, because the source digest still refuses. The semantic kill is the profile-2 shared-CID test
    (left: None).
  - A-cancelled (EXPLICIT AUTHOR SURVIVOR, retained) still PASSES the entire author suite, as the author
    recorded. That suite is not evidence of prompt interruption. My probes kill it:
    - RP10a: Invalid("issuer proof") instead of Cancelled, i.e. semantic work ran after cancellation.
    - RP10b: latency 1.40 s against a 1.75 s member stage.
    - RP10d: worst 388 ms against a 110 ms object hash.
- Reviewer controls:
  - Semantic kills found ONLY by reviewer probes (the author suite survives each):
    - R01 historical receipt issuer (RP04)
    - R02 source tip (RP05)
    - R08 null coordinates for membership keys (RP01, RP02)
    - R10 static writer (RP09)
    - R11 plan scope/issuer binding (RP06)
    - R12 hash unchunked and R13 no per-chunk poll (RP10d, timing; worst 82–85 ms against a ~110 ms hash)
    - R17 non-empty validity rule (RP15)
  - Author-suite LABEL-ONLY, semantic only with reviewer probes:
    - R05 retained-reference membership. The author tests use complete copies, where the digest refuses; RP16
      partial gives left: None.
    - R09 writer predecessor. The author test has bytes present, so the writer request refuses; RP17 with
      bytes missing gives left: None.
  - Semantic kills by the author suite:
    - R04 service slot
    - R06 partial untracked object
    - R07 proof purpose (via the Python profile-2 retained-purpose vector)
    - R16 full-flag
  - Label-only, layered: R18 record position. The issuer-proof chain refuses first, and MemberFraming.record
    re-checks contiguity.
  - SURVIVORS:
    - R03 slot-conflict map: an EQUIVALENT/redundant guard. slot = SHA-256(op), and (writer, op) is already
      unique (:366-369), so (writer, slot) can never recur without a hash collision.
    - R14 the initial poll in Work::new: EQUIVALENT. The first input/check poll precedes all work.
    - R15 the 44-byte membership input charge: accounting only and unpinned by any test. An input-budget edge
      over membership would pin it.

Findings A
- A-F1 [MEDIUM — design incoherence, implementation follows one side. Resolve before any creation writer signs
  `unavailable`.]
  - The codec has two rules that contradict each other:
    - codec :165-166: "wrong length/hash produces corrupt entries".
    - codec :406-408, the governing checkpoint: "A hash-valid request that fails its writer signature or exact
      manifest binding is invalid member evidence, not a repairable missing-byte condition".
  - The code folds the length check into byte validity (:447-449). It never reaches writer/manifest
    verification for a hash-valid object whose issuer-signed length is false.
  - RP14a shows genuine original request bytes reported as Corrupt, with the member accepted. The fault is
    attributed to the raw bytes, not to the false signed metadata.
  - Consequences:
    - A future observer would sign an `unavailable: corrupt` statement about authentic bytes.
    - The coordinate can never be restored, since any CID-matching candidate has the "wrong" length.
  - No false completion or publication is possible: there is no consumer, and publication re-verifies.
  - Same class, also accepted as a loss:
    - RP14b, an empty-CID with a positive signed length.
    - Signed lengths above evidence_service MAX_REQUEST (2 MiB + 4 KiB, src/evidence_service.rs:14-15), which no
      valid service request can have.
  - Required: decide which rule governs. For hash-valid bytes with a disagreeing authenticated length, refusing
    as invalid member evidence matches the checkpoint text and the north star (do not misattribute raw data).
    Then pin it in both implementations.
- A-F2 [LOW-MEDIUM — authentication gap in a reported projection]
  - Partial profile-3 membership is unauthenticated: the plan digest needs every source commit (RP02;
    copied.rs:200-203 has the same property).
  - Member.losses() nevertheless emits null coordinates and expected lengths derived from it.
  - The only signal is recipe_metadata_complete()==false. The loss entries themselves do not say which
    coordinates are authenticated.
  - Codec :103-105 says expectedLength comes "from authenticated metadata/membership".
  - Partial members cannot publish in KNB1, but a creation writer would still sign these coordinates.
  - Required before creation:
    - EITHER mark membership-only coordinates in partial members as unauthenticated, or withhold them,
    - OR state in the design that partial-copy membership is attested only by the external copy job.
- A-F3 [LOW — early-detectable impossibility deferred]: shared request CIDs across distinct (writer, op)
  occurrences (RP03) are accepted when the bytes are missing.
  - Static service requests make this unsatisfiable: the request bytes fix one operation and position.
  - Codec :157-158 deliberately keeps per-occurrence coordinates, and the Member claims no recoverability, so
    this is consistent but weak.
  - Consider refusing it outright for the service-request payload profile.
- A-F4 [LOW — test pinning]
  - The author suite does not pin these guards:
    - early/prompt cancellation (the retained survivor)
    - historical receipt issuer
    - source tip
    - plan scope/issuer binding
    - static writer
    - null coordinates for unreferenced membership keys
    - partial retained-membership
    - writer predecessor without bytes
    - empty-CID orphan
    - chunked member hashing
  - Production code is correct on each (probes above). Promote RP01, RP04-RP07, RP09, RP10a, RP15-RP17
    (deterministic), and keep RP10b/RP10d as recorded timing evidence. A deterministic member-stage hook,
    analogous to scope B's, would replace them.
- A-F5 [INFO]
  - Redundant/equivalent guards: R03, R14, R18 (layered).
  - Unpinned accounting: R15.
  - Membership length 0 refuses with the label "forensic-recovery-required" (:207-211). The refusal is
    correct; the label is misleading.
  - The caller duty to refuse non-canonical physical CID text lives only in the design (codec :389-390), not in
    the module rustdoc. The DASL parser itself refuses uppercase (RP13).

Scope-narrowing (Step 4): the diff's "remain separate work" / "pending" lines (codec :412-414, :417-422) defer
greedy partitioning, replay, checkpoints, schema and storage. Those were named BEFORE this checkpoint (codec
:305-310), so the deferral is legitimate, not drift. No other narrowing language was found
(logs: grep in transcript; command in COMMANDS context).
Forbidden patterns:
- No store mutation, subject destruction, blocking hook, second UI or cites manipulation.
- Persistence surface unchanged, so no read-write-surface.tsv obligation.
- Raw corrupt/empty/orphan bytes are retained verbatim in M1. A-F1 is a mis-projection, not a collapse of raw
  data.

writer.

- Evidence: src :1-2, :76-82; no fs/rusqlite in the module; lib.rs:32 is the only reference.

- Verdict: met.

- Verdict: met.
- Evidence: :344-354. RP09; R10 is killed (by the reviewer only).

- Verdict: met.

SCOPE A VERDICT: **APPROVE WITH FOLLOW-UPS**
The verifier is a sound, bounded, pure checkpoint. Every guard I attacked either refuses correctly or is a
demonstrated equivalent. Cancellation and deadlines are prompt, and the M1/loss output matches an independent
signed construction. It confers no history, recoverability or publication authority. It is not BLOCK because
nothing consumes it and no invariant is violated.
Required before creation signs `unavailable` events:

  corrupt under false signed lengths.
- A-F2 leaves partial-copy loss coordinates unauthenticated without saying so per entry.

semantically pinned only by reviewer probes, not by the author suite.

B. FRAMING FOLLOW-THROUGH (99f1fba)

- No non-test runtime change: CONFIRMED.
  - `git diff 61b8667 99f1fba -- src/` is +76/-0, in evidence_recovery_commitment.rs only.

- RA3/RA4 promotion is FAITHFUL: whitespace-normalised token streams equal the original reviewer functions,
  and the helpers are identical apart from emit, which now writes to stderr (logs/30).
- Polling units are meaningful, deterministic evidence of bounded interruption granularity:
  - They drive the real MemberFraming::original_object and RestorationFraming::candidate.
  - They inject cancellation when charged bytes reach a threshold, with no sleeps and no host-speed skip.
  - They assert exact charged deltas (60 + 65536 and 65536) and poisoning.
- The 13 follow-up controls, reproduced from the tracked reviewer-cases.json (cmd/controls_b.py,
  mutations/scope-b/, logs/40):
  - All 13 are KILLED by semantic assertions.
  - AC01: left Ok(()) vs Err(Cancelled). AC02: 4194304 vs 65536 charged.
  - AC25: both units fail.

- B7 no non-test runtime change: met.

SCOPE B VERDICT: **APPROVE WITH FOLLOW-UPS** (B-F1 and B-F3 are trivial; B-F2 restates the prior A-F4 limit
for deadlines).

- logs/10 (…ATTEMPT1) and logs/11 (…ATTEMPT2): probe construction errors.

content.text:
The review is finished and the report is at `review-evidence/REPORT.txt`. Scope A gets **APPROVE WITH FOLLOW-UPS**, Scope B gets **APPROVE WITH FOLLOW-UPS**, and so does the overall verdict. This covers the logical-member checkpoint only; none of the parent design's acceptance criteria (AC-1 to AC-6) is met.

**Custody.** Before and after the review, the export matched the frozen manifest and the git blobs at 5e54513: 3108 files, 0 mismatches, with `north-star.json` and `review-evidence/` the only extras. My temporary probe files in `tests/` were removed after confirming identical copies are in `review-evidence/probes/`. Every source mutation was restored and hash-checked. I made no git, kan or day writes; the recording is the report file.

**Baseline.** I reproduced the author's numbers: 33 integration tests (16 member, 8 commitment, 2 promoted, 7 observation) and the 2 polling units pass. Strict Clippy and fmt are clean, and both Python fixture checks pass. This held both before and after all mutations.

**Scope A: member verifier**
- **A-F1 (medium, fix before any creation writer):** the design contradicts itself. One rule (codec.md:165-166) says a wrong length means "corrupt". The checkpoint rule (codec.md:406-408) says a hash-valid request whose signed metadata doesn't match is invalid member evidence, not a repairable loss. The code follows the first rule (src/evidence_recovery_member.rs:447-449). My probe RP14a gives genuine request bytes with a false, issuer-signed length: the member is accepted and the bytes are reported as `Corrupt`. A future observer would then sign a corruption claim about authentic bytes, and that entry can never be restored.
- **A-F2 (low-medium):** in a partial profile-3 copy, the membership list isn't authenticated by anything. Fabricated keys are still reported as losses with made-up lengths, and dropped keys go unnoticed (RP02). Only `recipe_metadata_complete()==false` signals this; the loss entries themselves don't say which coordinates are unauthenticated.
- **A-F3 (low):** two records pointing at the same request CID are accepted while the bytes are missing (RP03). Once the genuine bytes are supplied, the member refuses, so no restoration can ever satisfy it.
- **A-F4 (test gaps; the code itself is correct on each):**
  - The author's early-cancellation survivor is retained: removing that guard still passes the whole author suite.
  - My probes kill it: a pre-cancelled call runs on to a semantic error. Cancellation latency jumps from about 1 ms to 1.4 s, or 388 ms against a single 110 ms object hash.
  - The author suite also misses five more guards that only my probes catch: historical receipt issuer, source tip, plan scope/issuer binding, static writer, and null losses for unreferenced membership keys.
  - Two more author kills are label-only: the input is still refused, just with a different reason. My probes RP16 and RP17 kill them semantically.
- **Mutants that survive everything:** R03 (slot-conflict map) and R14 (initial poll) are equivalent to the original code. R15 (the membership byte charge) is accounting that no test pins.

**Scope B: framing follow-through (99f1fba)**
- It adds no production runtime code: the `src/` change is +76/-0 and every addition is gated behind `#[cfg(test)]`.
- The promoted RA3/RA4 tests are identical to the originals apart from formatting.
- The polling tests are deterministic, with no sleeps or skips. All 13 follow-up controls fail on real assertions when I re-run them. My extra mutants that poll every 128 KiB instead of 64 KiB are also caught.
- Follow-ups:
  - **B-F1:** Rust has no multibyte issuer-length test, so counting characters instead of bytes survives. The Python oracle does catch it.
  - **B-F2:** deadline polling is still only covered by the earlier timing-based probe.
  - **B-F3:** the regression file's header comment cites vector provenance that doesn't apply.

**Process notes.**
- My first two probe runs and one Python mutant run failed because of my own construction errors; those logs are kept.
- The permission mode denied one combined cleanup command. I re-ran its steps one at a time and all passed, except the parent worktree `git status`, which I didn't retry. The manifest and git-blob check covers integrity instead.
- The RP10 cancellation and deadline probes are timing-based, with margins of 25× or more on this machine.

Remaining full-bundle work, listed in the report:
- splitting the loss list into signed ≤32-entry / 16 KiB unavailable events
- observation replay
- historical restoration-candidate selection
- output revalidation and the publication rules
- external checkpoints
- the physical schema, opener, UTF-8 check and CID-text reader
- creation, restoration and publication writers with crash tests
- bundle backup and rebuild
- owner jobs, RPC and UI
